text:
Artyom Levshunov, the second overall pick in 2024, hasn't recorded a point in 15 straight games. That's the headline, and it would be easier to call it bad luck if the chances were there. They mostly aren't: 4.3 expected points over the drought, and the chances have thinned out.

Chicago gets 39% of the expected goals with him on at five on five, a hard number even on a team that struggles to control play. Evolving-Hockey's note from last season is the context: he played with some of the weakest teammates in the league, which drags raw numbers down. The flip side was that opponents got far more chances with him on the ice.

There's an athlete in here. NHL Edge has him in the 80s percentile for top speed and bursts, and Mark Lazerus of The Athletic noted he saved a goal in Calgary on Nov 21. At 21 he's playing over 20 minutes a night.

Defensemen picked in the top four almost always become NHL regulars (16 of 17 with four seasons reached 200 games). What to watch: a first point, and then whether the defensive numbers move.
